input.question: What is net neutrality?
input.ground_truth: Net neutrality is the concept that every internet service provider *(ISP)* treats every piece of data equally. This means that the ISP doesn't slow packages down when they go to websites that aren't in their favor. This means that ISP A transfers the packages of its own customers just as reliably and just as fast as the packages coming from or going to ISP B. In a nutshell. Internet transfer is equal for everybody

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine the internet is like a big playground with lots of slides, swings, and sandboxes. Now, imagine the people who run the playground (like your parents or teachers) want to make sure that **everybody** can use all the playground equipment the same way. That means you can go on any slide, swing, or sandbox whenever you want, and nobody can tell you, "Oh, you can't go on that slide unless you pay extra!"

**Net neutrality** is a rule that says the people who help the internet work (like the companies that give us the internet) have to treat all the games and websites the same. They can't make some websites go slower, or charge you more money to visit your favorite site, just because they want to.

So, **net neutrality is like making sure everyone gets to play fair on the internet playground!**
